feed.title: Windhawk Mod Updates
feed.subtitle: Updates in the official collection of Windhawk mods

entry.title: Mac Island & Dock 3.2.0
entry.content:
New

  • Your commands can run by themselves: give a command a time and days in its editor ("Run by itself, at a time") and it runs while the island is on, as a click would. A notice says if it ran or couldn't, with Try again and, for a command line, Open in terminal. The schedules are looked at once a minute on the island's thread (CheckScheduledCommands): CommandMinutesDue runs the minute it is in (the first one too, and after a sleep) and, at a summer-time change, the minutes the clock skipped (UTC one minute on, the zone in daylight time, the jump its bias), never one twice, also across a restart in the same minute; nothing missed is made up. A failed command line's output is kept for its notice's Open in terminal, which shows it (type) instead of running the line again.
  • The graphics card's use and temperature can go on the pill, next to CPU, RAM and VRAM; a click opens the GPU tab of the usage panel (Apps and tools tab).
  • The charging battery's color can be green as before, like the other icons, Windows' accent or one you pick (System tab, #6816).
  • A Mobile data tile in the control center, only on a PC with a mobile broadband modem; add it with Edit (#6888).
  • A short notice with the cover, title and artist when the song changes; a click opens What's playing (What's playing tab, off by default, #6822).
  • The wheel on what's playing can go the other way round: up is the next song (What's playing tab, off by default, #6822).
  • A banner can close when you click anywhere outside it and the island; calls, alarms and reminders stay until you answer them (Banners tab, off by default, #6822).
  • The Bar can hide to its line too (#7131): with "Hide as its line" and the new "Bar: hide as its line too" on, the Bar shrinks to a thin line on the screen's edge when the mouse is away, and comes back as the mouse reaches the line. Windows then use the strip it kept, and the Bar shows over them.
  • In the Bar, the items can go to the screen's corners without the clock in the middle, like the macOS menu bar: put a separator line in the order (+ Line) and, with "Bar: items at the screen's corners" on and the clock not in the middle, the items before the first line stay at the left corner and the rest, the clock too, at the right one.
  • Help translate: a button in the language section (General tab) saves every text of the island in a file to translate into your language, or to review the one you use, and send in a new issue. A language with a reviewer says who. The file is written by the backup thread (BackupThreadProc), as the settings backup is.
  • A Share button on the shelf (and on each file under the mouse) opens Windows' own share window: Nearby sharing, Phone Link, Quick Share and the other targets (#7133). It's Windows' share UI for the island's window (IDataTransferManagerInterop::ShowShareUIForWindow), with the files as StorageFiles.
  • GlazeWM's workspaces can go on the pill, a dot each (the one shown lit, the ones with windows faint; a click switches), like komorebi's; "Hide the workspaces without windows" leaves out the empty ones (Control center tab, #7116). GlazeWM's own IPC, a WebSocket on 127.0.0.1:6123 (WinHTTP), only while the item is on.
  • Faísca, a little light that lives on the pill (#7045): an item of its own in every style, and on the minimized line too. Her eyes follow the mouse and change shape with how she feels (happy, angry, sad, startled, sleepy...), she blinks, does little things by herself, dances with the music of the apps you check and reacts to the PC (working hard, a low battery, Do not disturb, notifications, files copied, downloads, screenshots, the volume, USB, the charger, Wi-Fi, the song, Pomodoro, reminders), each reaction with its own switch. Her size can be chosen, her glow can leave the island (also over a maximized app) and the pill glows with her. All her options are in her own tab. There also: her color (eight, Windows' accent or your own, optionally changing with her mood), her personality (calm, normal or lively) and the processor use from which she counts the PC as working hard. She's drawn with Direct2D like the rest of the island, and her frames come from her own timer, only while she moves (about 30 a second, none when she's still).
  • Live activities like the iPhone's Dynamic Island (#7134). In Banners, turn on Live activities: the system alerts (charger, low battery, Bluetooth with the headset's battery, Do not disturb, desktop) show as a wide compact pill with the icon in a colored circle and the value at the right end, and optionally the apps' notifications in the same compact layout. And, with Expanded card, the mouse resting on what's live (the music, a timer or the stopwatch, a download or a copy) grows the pill in place into its card: the cover with the title, a bar and the buttons, the big time with pause and cancel, or the percent.
  • Five small games with Faísca (fruit rain, on the beat, cloud jump, island memory, reflex), with your best results kept on this PC.
  • Faísca's panel: click her to see her big, pet her with the mouse, tap her (not too often: she gets cross), read what she has to say, and open her games. Optional care: energy, food, water and love go down slowly while you use the PC, and you feed her, give her water and cuddle her there (she never goes away and never asks in full screen or Do not disturb). How fast they go down is a setting (calm, normal or attentive).
  • Sounds for Faísca, off until you turn them on: 25 sounds she makes (eating, a tap, a finished download, a plugged-in charger...), each with its own switch and its own source: the island's own, a pack downloaded when you choose it, or a file of yours. They stay silent over full-screen apps and with Do not disturb on. Her volume has its own slider. The island's own sounds are made by the mod and played with waveOut; a file of yours is decoded with Media Foundation, loaded only then. The pack comes from jsDelivr pinned to a commit (cesarkali/faisca-sounds@cec274c, CC BY 4.0), each file kept only if its SHA-256 is the one in the mod (BCryptHash), downloaded only when chosen. Never in full screen or Do not disturb.
  • What's playing: shuffle and repeat buttons (repeat all, then repeat one with a small 1, then off) in every look of the panel, shown only when the playing app supports them, like Spotify (thanks Jawad). From the media session's PlaybackInfo (IsShuffleActive, AutoRepeatMode), changed with TryChangeShuffleActiveAsync and TryChangeAutoRepeatModeAsync, shown only when Controls.IsShuffleEnabled/IsRepeatEnabled.
  • Faísca's panel says why she is as she is ("Dancing · Spotify is playing", "Hot · the processor at 92%", "Asleep · no mouse or keyboard for 6 min") and what she reacted to lately, with the time and her sound then: its name, or why it was silent.
  • A bubble saying when Num Lock turns on or off, like the Caps Lock one (Banners tab, off by default, #7178).
  • The processor's temperature can go on the pill, next to CPU use, only when Windows itself reports it (many desktops don't; Apps and tools tab, off by default). Read with PDH (\Thermal Zone Information(*)\Temperature, PdhAddEnglishCounter); without a thermal zone the item hides. No driver and no extra DLL.
  • What's playing's panel: two new options leave out the volume sliders with the mixer, and the two pill switches at its end, for a panel with only the player (thanks Jawad).
  • The timer and Pomodoro can fill the pill with color as the time runs out: orange, green on a break, fainter when paused, a soft pulse at the end, in every style and on the minimized line. Hide the numbers keeps only the icon on the pill, so the fill is all you see.
  • The Bar can have three parts: put two separator lines in the order (+ Line) with "Bar: items at the screen's corners" on, and the items before the first line stay at the left corner, the ones between the lines in the middle of the screen (the clock joins them when it is in the middle) and the rest at the right corner.
  • Tasks can have a date (#7195): turn on "Dates on tasks" and pick a day in the task's editor (Today, Tomorrow or any day). The day shows under the task, red when it passed, and the dated tasks come first. With "Tasks with a date in the calendar" on, the calendar marks those days with a small dash and lists the tasks in the day's list, where a click on the circle completes them.
  • Copy verification codes: a notification with a one-time code (like a sign-in or a bank code) gets a Copy code button on its banner and in the list. The code goes to the clipboard and stays out of its history (Notifications tab, off by default, #6997).
  • Faísca has fun too: with her care and her games on, a fifth vial that goes down while nobody plays with her. Bored and later sad, she now and then asks to play with two little hops and a pleading look on the pill (at most every 30 minutes, never in full screen, in Do not disturb or over a notification; it has its own switch). A round of a game cheers her up a lot, petting or a tap a little, dancing to music a tiny bit.
  • The island speaks French (Français), Turkish (Türkçe) and Korean (한국어), Windhawk's settings page too: choose one in the General tab, or it follows Windows. The first French texts are by 11ethann11 (#7063, #7186, #7228). The texts stay in the source, in the same packed tables as the other languages.

Improvements

  • The volume's percentage sits as close to its icon as the battery's (#6199).
  • The Bluetooth "Connected" notice shows the headset's battery when Windows knows it, like "Galaxy Buds2" with "Connected · 80%" under it (#6158).
  • Windows 11 only, 64-bit (x64 and ARM64): Windows 10, whose support Microsoft ended in October 2025, and 32-bit Windows are no longer supported.
  • Faísca costs much less while she moves: only the small area around her is drawn again and sent to the screen, not the whole island (in the Bar, the whole strip), on every monitor. Her area (m_petArea) is the only part cleared, drawn (an aliased axis-aligned clip, the rest of the bitmap kept) and presented (UpdateLayeredWindowIndirect with prcDirty) on her own frames.
  • If the island crashes and can't be started again by itself (on Windhawk 2.0, or after three crashes in ten minutes), a window says so and how to start it again: turn the mod off and on in Windhawk. It waits until a full-screen game or presentation is over. A TaskDialogIndirect on its own thread in Explorer, closed when the mod unloads. It only tells (nothing is started from it), and only for an island process whose image is Windhawk's.
  • With "Glow and hops can leave the island" on (or her size over 100%), each of her frames draws only her own window, no longer the whole island again behind her. The island remembers that her window was drawn alone (m_petWindowLast) and takes the full path again whenever anything else changes.

Fixes

  • Windows builds without the parts the dock uses (some Insider builds): the taskbar stays as Windows draws it and the island's taskbar parts (apps asking for attention, the screen-edge watch, the tray icons) now start right away, instead of waiting two minutes and giving up (#7241). ApplyToTaskbar counts a missing TaskbarFrame (g_dockUnavailable) as ready, so StartTaskbarParts runs (#7241).
  • Win+A and Win+N with Windows' own quick settings or notification center open now let Windows close them, instead of opening the island's control center or notifications over them (#7226). With an app run as administrator in front (Task Manager), Windows doesn't send the keys to the island at all: they work there only when Windhawk runs as administrator too. WindowsPanelInFront looks for Windows' own flyout before the island opens its panel.
  • The input method's bubble no longer shows up by itself when an app opens or is busy: when the app doesn't answer in time, the island keeps what it showed instead of taking it for English letters (#7260). The input method's state is asked with a time limit; with no answer the last known one stays.
  • A banner's title too long for its place keeps its "..." under the mouse until it starts scrolling, instead of being cut in the middle of a word.
  • Night light on a PC where it was never set up in Windows: the tile says Set up instead of Unavailable, and a click (also on the pill's button) opens Windows' Night light page with a short notice, since Windows only applies it after that first time.
  • Scrolling the settings window uses much less of the graphics card (#7282): dimmed switches and cards no longer draw a layer as big as the whole window on every frame, and the window draws at most about 60 frames a second. The dimmed parts' layers are bound to the visible area and the window's frames are capped.
  • The Wi-Fi panel, the control center's network tile and the pill's Wi-Fi icon show the connected network and its signal without location access too: only the list of nearby networks needs it (#7155). The connected network comes from WlanQueryInterface (wlan_intf_opcode_current_connection); where Windows refuses it without location access, the connection's profile stands in (NetworkInformation, GetConnectedSsid and GetSignalBars, read on a thread of its own). Only the nearby networks (WlanGetAvailableNetworkList) still need the location.
  • Tray icons of apps that run as administrator (many antivirus apps) now open with a click on the island even when Windhawk itself runs as administrator, and when an app still doesn't get a click, the log says which one.
  • The audio visualizer's bars now leave the pill when the player closes, instead of staying there until something else plays.
  • "Hide the Windows banners" is no longer greyed out while "The island handles notifications and their sounds" is on: it still hides the Windows banners that come through Do not disturb (calls, alarms, priority apps), so it can be turned off there too.
  • The What's playing panel opened from the visualizer once the player is closed shows "Nothing playing" on its own, without the last song's cover and artist (#7301).
  • The island no longer freezes for a moment when Windows is slow to say whether an app is in full screen: it asks on a separate thread and uses the last answer. SHQueryUserNotificationState sends a message to Explorer and waited up to ~400 ms in Island::Tick -> IsFullscreenAppOn up to 15 times a minute (all the islands share one thread), found by sampling the thread. Now the island asks on a thread-pool thread at most every 250 ms (TrySubmitThreadpoolCallback) and the callers use the last answer; the explorer part still asks directly.
  • The Bar no longer stays one strip below the top of the screen after a game changes the resolution (like 4:3) and back: the strip it keeps is set again for the screen's new size. The monitor rect the AppBar was set for is kept at ABM_SETPOS; Island::Render compares it with the monitor's now and sets the position again (SetAppBarPosition, Layout) when it changed.
  • With "The island handles notifications and their sounds" on, a reminder, call or alarm that Windows lets through Do not disturb (like a web app's notification that stays until closed) no longer shows Windows' own banner next to the island's while the pill is minimized or auto-hidden with "Banners even with the pill minimized" on: the island takes it over there too, with Windows' buttons. Chromium sends a notification that stays until closed as scenario="reminder", and Do not disturb's priority profile lets reminders through. The takeover decision (TakesOverBanner, used by CanTakeOverAhead and WantsTakeover) now also allows a minimized or auto-hidden pill when "Banners even with the pill minimized" is on, and minimizing or hiding ends a takeover that no longer applies.
  • The settings window's minimize, maximize and close buttons work again while the window is maximized (#7358): a click on them is now taken where Windows draws them, at the top right, and the middle one puts the window back. DwmDefWindowProc doesn't find the caption buttons of a maximized window with a custom frame. While IsZoomed, the panel answers WM_NCHITTEST and the WM_NCLBUTTON* messages itself for the 46 DIP buttons at the client's right edge (SC_MINIMIZE, SC_RESTORE, SC_CLOSE).
  • The dock no longer closes the Start button's right-click menu (Win+X) when the mouse moves fast from the dock to its options. It stays up and keeps the focus while a taskbar menu is open (#7360). GetGUIThreadInfo on the taskbar's thread (GUI_INMENUMODE, GUI_POPUPMENUMODE) for Win32 menus, and on newer builds a shown Xaml_WindowedPopupClass window on that thread while it's in front (the Win+X menu is a XAML menu there): while a menu is open the hide timer tries again every 300 ms. Only with auto-hide on.
  • "What's playing on the minimized line" now follows "Apps that bring the visualizer": with apps chosen there, the line's cover and bars show only while one of them is heard, not for any sound (#7343). MusicLineWanted asks the same chosen-apps list as the visualizer (MusicLinePlays).
  • "Apps that bring the visualizer" no longer lists one app twice when the media controls and Windows' audio know it under different names (Yandex Music had two cards): the card with the app's own icon stays, with your choice (#7301). Each audio session also keeps its packaged app ID and its Start menu name (read once per process), and a heard session joins the card of the same app.
  • On the left and right notches (Corners and Three), the minimized line stays near its corner instead of moving away when the notch grows, like while music plays (#7359). Island::LineMiddle keeps the line's middle at most 24 px (scaled) plus half the hovered line from the corner, as long as it fits in the notch; the small pill on the line follows it.
  • Explorer no longer crashes at sign-in on some PCs when the mod reaches the taskbar before Windows has finished making it (#7310). The 3.1.1 x64 fault offset (0x6b90) is XamlRootFromTaskbarHostSharedPtr reading a TaskbarHost that wasn't there yet; the chain (the TaskbarHost, its IUnknown, the TaskBand) is now checked for null, so the taskbar is left alone until it's ready.
  • The virtual desktops item no longer lists desktops closed long ago: on some PCs it showed extra ones that Windows still remembered, and renaming could pick the wrong desktop. In the island's elevated process the registry's VirtualDesktopIDs kept two desktops closed days before, while Explorer and other programs read one. With more than one ID read, each is checked with the desktops service's FindDesktop (already used for renaming, builds 26100+) on the watch thread: unknown ones are left out, the current one always stays, and all stay when the service knows none. Renaming takes the row's ID from the list shown.
  • With "Your own colors", the icons of the control center's switches that are on stay readable: a light highlight now gets a dark icon, instead of a white icon on white (#7431). The icon on a switch that is on is drawn in AccentInk (dark on a light highlight), as the other highlights' texts already were, not in the text color.

entry.title: Independent taskbar per monitor 1.7.0
entry.content:
• Fixed: window buttons of windows parked off-screen could appear on the taskbar of the leftmost monitor.
  • Fixed: clicking a pin could freeze the taskbar while the app's minimized window was busy.
  • Setting titles start with their section (Windows, Pins, Click, Animation).
  • Settings are available in English, German, Russian, French and Spanish.

entry.title: OverhauldedWin Alt+Tab 1.3.2
entry.content:
Added

  • Arrange open windows in an adaptive grid instead of the traditional horizontal carousel.
  • Automatically organizes cards into balanced rows, using up to four columns when space allows.
  • Grid: Navigate between cards using the arrow keys, with smooth selection animations.
  • Smooth scrolling with indicators when additional rows are available.
  • Added System, Dark and Light themes. System automatically follows the Windows app theme.

Improved

  • Window management:
  • Added smooth card repositioning when the window list or layout changes.
  • Improved selected-card scaling and visual transitions.
  • Refined the shared transparent background surface.
  • Improved the restoration of minimized windows when activating them.
  • Improved screen-coordinate handling for mouse interactions.

Other changes

  • Added additional activation diagnostics.
  • Improved timer error handling and logging.
  • Updated settings and documentation.
  • Added the required Windows system library dependency.

entry.title: Taskbar System Utilities 1.3
entry.content:
• Custom Menu Items: Added support for launching custom programs, files, folders, scripts, URLs, ms-settings: pages, and shell: locations directly from the Windows 11 taskbar context menu (includes Terminal and Control Panel by default).
  • Rich Item Customization: Each custom entry supports environment variable expansion (e.g., %USERPROFILE%), optional command-line arguments, Segoe Fluent Icons hex glyphs or emojis, Run as administrator (UAC elevation), Hide window, separator lines (-), and disabled section headings (items without a command).
  • Flexible Menu Layout & Submenus: Added options to place custom items below built-in items (bottom), above them (top), or inside the System Utilities submenu (submenu), group custom items into their own dedicated submenu with a custom name and icon, and choose top or bottom placement for System Utilities.
  • Improved Unload Lifecycle: Added weak-reference tracking for injected menu items and click handlers to cleanly detach and hide elements when the mod is unloaded or updated.

entry.title: Background Dimmer 1.1.1
entry.content: • Hotkeys now need Win plus at least one of Ctrl, Alt or Shift, so a hotkey can't take over typing keys (Shift+letter) or the Win+letter keys Windows uses. Saved hotkeys that don't follow this stop working and must be set again.

entry.title: Taskbar Active Window Highlight 0.1.1
entry.content:
Taskbar Active Window Highlight

When an app has several windows, Windows 11's thumbnail preview gives no hint about which one is active. This mod adds an accent-colored highlight to the active window's card. The taskbar button keeps Windows' native indicator.

Requires the Windows 11 taskbar's XAML thumbnail previews (tested on Windows 11 build 26300). With the classic thumbnails, or with StartAllBack or ExplorerPatcher, the mod has no effect.

How it works

The mod does not track focus itself. It reads the state Explorer already keeps:

  • The taskbar's active task item (TaskbarAppsList.ActiveItem), which names the active window. The mod follows Explorer's own change notifications.
  • Each thumbnail card's view model, which names the window the card shows.

The highlight is a separate element placed right above the card's own background, below the title, icon and preview image. Its size and corner radius are bound to that background, so it follows themes such as Windows 11 Taskbar Styler.

Clicking the taskbar or a preview list briefly moves focus to the taskbar itself. By default the last active window stays highlighted until another window or the desktop takes focus, or the window is minimized or closed.

How it differs from Taskbar Recent Focus Highlight

Taskbar Recent Focus Highlight ranks apps and windows by recent use, from its own focus history. This mod answers a narrower question, which window is active right now, by reading Explorer's own active task item, with no focus tracking of its own. While another app has focus it marks nothing in this app's preview, and it also marks single-window previews.

Performance and footprint

  • Event-driven only. No background thread, timers, polling or focus tracking. The mod runs only when Explorer reports a new active window or binds a preview card to a window.
  • Nothing on hover or layout. Moving the mouse over the taskbar or previews runs no mod code.
  • Under 1 ms, usually about 0.01 ms. Measured in normal use: typical 0.004–0.013 ms per event, worst case 0.67 ms (the first time a card's highlight is created).
  • One element per card, created once and then only shown or hidden.
  • Safe to unload. No event handlers are left in Explorer, so disabling the mod cleanly removes it.

entry.title: 1 Letter Language Indicator 1.0
entry.content:
1 Letter Language Indicator

Simplifies the input language indicator in the Windows 11 taskbar tray to a single letter: ENG becomes E, and ENG (US) becomes E.

The indicator keeps updating when you switch input languages, and the original text is restored when the mod is disabled.

Settings

  • Letter size: the font size of the letter. Set it to 0 to keep the Windows size (12).
  • Letter color: separate colors for light mode and dark mode, chosen by the taskbar's theme (the Windows mode). Each one can be:
    • A hex color (#RRGGBB or #AARRGGBB) or a color name (Red, White).
    • accent for the Windows accent color, or one of its shades: accentLight1 to accentLight3, accentDark1 to accentDark3. The letter follows accent color changes.
    • Empty, to keep the Windows color in that mode.
  • Vertical offset: moves the letter up (negative) or down (positive), in pixels. Useful for re-centering the letter after changing its size.
  • Indicator width: the language indicator normally reserves room for three letters. With a single letter that leaves empty space, so by default the indicator is narrowed to 32 pixels, the width of a regular tray icon. Set it to 0 to keep the Windows width.

Notes

  • Languages and layouts which start with the same letter look the same, e.g. ENG (US) and ENG (UK), or ENG and ESP.
  • Other mods may set the same properties. "Taskbar tray icon spacing and grid" sets the width of the language indicator: while Indicator width is set, this mod's width wins. Windows 11 Taskbar Styler themes which change the font size or color of the indicator conflict with Letter size and Letter color, and whichever mod applies last wins. To let the other mod control a property, set the matching setting to 0 (or leave the color empty).

Target

SystemTray.LanguageTextIconContent > Grid#ContainerGrid >
SystemTray.AdaptiveTextBlock#LanguageInnerTextBlock > TextBlock#InnerTextBlock

Only Windows 11 is supported.

entry.title: System Tray Folders 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Fixed the flyout's icon list not being found on Windows builds where it has no name.
  • Added a List view option that shows the flyout as one column with each icon's name next to it, plus List view width.
  • Added an Add icon... tile inside each folder that lists the tray icons by app name, shows which folder each one is in, and moves icons in or out with a click. Picks are remembered by the mod and take priority over the patterns.

entry.title: Fix file dialogs for Classic theme 2.0
entry.content: • Fix more dialogs

entry.title: WinTips OSD 1.6.1
entry.content:
• Added a solo-Shift inference fallback for the input language tip: third-party IMEs that never answer WM_IME_CONTROL now get their Chinese/English mode tracked by the classic solo Shift press-and-release gesture. A 350 ms grace window gives the system read a chance to report the toggle first; odd numbers of solo Shift releases flip the cached mode, even numbers settle silently, and Shift+letter, Alt+Shift and Ctrl+Shift all drop out of the gesture on their own. The inference only applies to Chinese IME layouts.
  • Caps Lock now opens the language watch as well, so IMEs that toggle Chinese/English with it (Weasel's default, Sogou's option) report the mode on the language card.
  • Copy, paste and cut tips no longer fire when Win is held: Win+Ctrl+V opens the Volume Mixer and Win+Ctrl+C toggles color filters. Ctrl+Shift+V stays a paste.
  • Updated the readme.

entry.title: Start Button Replacer 1.0.0
entry.content:
• Added SVG support for all image sources (local files and HTTP/HTTPS URLs ending in .svg). Only static SVG content is rendered.
  • Added optional Dark mode images that replace the main images while Windows is in dark mode. Blank fields use the main images, and images switch automatically when the Windows mode changes.
  • Image load warnings now show which settings group the failed image belongs to.
  • Added a Credits section to the readme. Thanks to Asteski for SVG support and dark mode images.

entry.title: Window Centralizer 1.2.0
entry.content:
• Windows shown with SetWindowPlacement are now centered. Programs that restore a saved position this way (7-Zip's file manager) were left where they were, whatever the size limit.
  • New option, Center on the unrelated launcher window (Parent mode only): a program started from another one, such as from Explorer's context menu or an archive opened from a folder, opens centered on the window it was started from (if inside the window size limit target). That window is the one in the foreground when the new process starts, and it must belong to the launching program (any Explorer process counts), so programs started from Start or the taskbar still open at the center of the monitor.
  • Hotkeys now require Win, at least one more modifier (Ctrl, Alt or Shift) and a key; other combinations are rejected, so a hotkey such as Shift+letter can't catch ordinary typing.

entry.title: Task Manager Pause Button 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Keeps Pause active when switching between Processes and Details, and resumes Task Manager updates when opening other pages.
  • Restores direct support for opening Task Manager on Details, using the available navigation symbols while avoiding duplicate hooks for shared function addresses.
  • Adds Frame.Navigated handling as a fallback for page detection and refresh-state changes.
  • Improves command-bar detection and retries button insertion when the toolbar is not ready.
  • Keeps the Pause/Resume button usable with its text label if the native icon cannot be created.
  • Improves cleanup of button and navigation event handlers when disabling the mod.

entry.title: Winstant 1.6
entry.content: -there’s a new setting, “Open the panel by hovering the minimize button” (Panel group). Turn it off and the panel opens only with the hotkey or key taps. The mouse wheel on the minimize button keeps its own option.

entry.title: Adobe Dark Menus 1.1.0
entry.content:
• Fixed a crash on exit, seen in InDesign and Audition.
  • Fixed the scroll arrows of long menus when Menu Background Color is mid gray or lighter.
  • Fixed submenus drawn by Windows taking the custom background of an app-drawn parent menu.
  • Fixed dark title bars on right-to-left windows.
  • Fixed a case where dropdown list colors could stay on after the list was gone.
  • No more arrow flicker after scrolling a long menu with the keyboard, and less work while the mouse moves over one.
  • Safer when the mod is turned off or updated while an app is running.
  • Added a Scroll Long Menus Instead of Columns setting, on by default: a menu an app splits into columns, such as the After Effects Effect menu with many plugins installed, now opens as one dark column that scrolls instead of staying light.
  • Added InCopy, Lightroom and Lightroom Classic.
  • Added the Beta versions of Premiere Pro, InDesign, InCopy and Audition.

entry.title: File Hover Info 1.2.0
entry.content:
• New option to show or hide file extensions in the card's name, or follow File Explorer's setting.
  • Shortcuts (.lnk, .url) no longer show their extension, as in File Explorer.

entry.title: Taskbar Thumbnail Stats 1.8
entry.content:
• New "RAM format" option: show the RAM as a size, as a percentage of the total RAM, or both
  • New "Show GPU" option (off by default): GPU usage in percent, computed like Task Manager and respecting "Include child processes"

entry.title: Taskbar AI Quota 2.21.2
entry.content:
• Add a chart for Anthropic extra usage to the details flyout, with its monthly reset time, pace and projected limit time.
  • Add an Extra usage chart setting to chart it over the month or the weekly window, or keep the bar.

entry.title: Explorer Item Pins 1.1.5
entry.content:
Explorer Item Pins

English · Русский

Explorer Item Pins keeps selected files and folders at the top of their parent folder in Windows File Explorer. Each folder has its own pins.

Features
  • Two ways to pin. Use the modern context menu or the pin button between Share and Delete on the command bar.
  • Sort and group. Pins stay at the top in either sort direction. With grouping on, they appear in the first group, Pinned. Explorer's sorting still applies within the group.
  • Pin indicator. A pushpin appears at the upper-right corner of the file or folder icon. It follows the icon size and works with thumbnails, lists, details, tiles and content view.
  • Interface languages. English, Russian, Spanish, German, Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified Chinese.

Platforms

Requires Windows 11 x64 or ARM64 with the tabbed File Explorer.

Data exchange

Pins are stored separately for each Windows account. Uninstalling the mod removes its pins. Replacing a file under the same name keeps its pin. A rename within the same folder can keep the pin when the mod can identify the original file. Copying or moving an item to another folder does not carry its pin with it.

Usage

  1. Select a file or folder and choose Pin in item pane in its context menu, or click the pin on the command bar.
  2. To remove the pin, select the item and choose Unpin from item pane or click the crossed-out pin on the command bar. The item returns to its usual position in the folder.

In Windhawk, open the mod's Settings to control these options independently. All three are enabled by default.

If the pin commands are missing from a File Explorer window that was already open when the mod was enabled or updated, reopen that window.

Setting Controls
Context menu command Pin and unpin in the context menu
Command bar button Pin and unpin on the File Explorer command bar
Pinned item indicator The pushpin on pinned file and folder icons

Links

  • Explorer Item Pins on GitHub
  • DSN Windhawk Mods
